question: Why did US wildlife officials clone a black-footed ferret from cells frozen in 1988?
answer: To recover lost genes. Every black-footed ferret alive descends from seven animals bred after the species was found clinging on in Wyoming in the 1980s. Willa, a female whose cells were frozen, left no descendants; her clone Elizabeth Ann, born in 2020, carries variation missing from every living ferret. A freezer became a founder.
move: Before a population shrinks further, save what its survivors have lost.
reference: US Fish and Wildlife Service, announcement of the first cloned black-footed ferret, Elizabeth Ann, February 2021
